citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian tangent-bundle conventions of the suppliers. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, $r_0>0$, and $\mathcal E=I\times(r_0,\infty)\times S^2$, where $S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ has its unit round metric $q_{AB}$ and area form $d\Omega$. Let $D_A$ be the Levi-Civita covariant derivative of $q$, and raise angular indices with $q^{AB}$. A **Bondi-Sachs end** is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $\mathcal E$ written in coordinates $(u,r,x^A)$, $A,B=1,2$, as

$$g=-\left(e^{2\beta}\frac Vr-r^2\gamma_{AB}U^AU^B\right)du^2-2e^{2\beta}du\,dr-2r^2\gamma_{AB}U^Bdu\,dx^A+r^2\gamma_{AB}dx^A dx^B,$$

where $\beta,V,U^A,\gamma_{AB}$ are smooth, $\gamma_{AB}$ is positive definite, $\gamma^{AC}\gamma_{CB}=\delta^A_B$, and $\det(\gamma_{AB})=\det(q_{AB})$. Thus $u=\mathrm{constant}$ are outgoing null hypersurfaces, $r$ is the area radius, and $x^A$ are constant along their null generators. This Bondi gauge has $g_{rr}=g_{rA}=0$.

A **smooth Bondi expansion** is such an end with the differentiated uniform expansions

$$\gamma_{AB}=q_{AB}+\frac{C_{AB}(u,x)}r+\frac{P_{AB}(u,x)}{r^2}+O(r^{-3}),\qquad \beta=O(r^{-2}),\qquad U^A=\frac{U^A_{(2)}(u,x)}{r^2}+\frac{U^A_{(3)}(u,x)}{r^3}+O(r^{-4}),\qquad V=r-2m(u,x)+\frac{V_{(1)}(u,x)}r+O(r^{-2}).$$

Here $C_{AB}$, $P_{AB}$ and the displayed coefficients are smooth sphere fields on $I$; the determinant gauge imposes $q^{AB}C_{AB}=0$ and $q^{AB}P_{AB}=\tfrac12 C_{AB}C^{AB}$. For every compact $I'\subset I$, angular chart compact set, and derivative multi-index $\alpha$ of total order at most two, the partial derivatives of each $O(r^{-k})$ remainder obey $\partial_u^{\alpha_u}D^{\alpha_x}\partial_r^{\alpha_r}O(r^{-k})=O(r^{-k-\alpha_r})$ uniformly as $r\to\infty$. Define the **mass aspect** $m$ by the $r^{-1}$ coefficient in $V$, the **Bondi shear** by $C_{AB}=\lim_{r\to\infty}r(\gamma_{AB}-q_{AB})$, the **Bondi news** by $N_{AB}:=\partial_u C_{AB}$, and the **geometric Bondi mass** by $m_B(u):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}m(u,x)\,d\Omega$. The future null boundary used here is the formal $r\to\infty$ boundary $\mathcal I^+=I\times S^2$ with coordinates $(u,x^A)$; no conformal completion is included in this definition. A **vacuum Bondi expansion** means, in addition, that the Ricci tensor $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ defined by the curvature convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] vanishes to the asymptotic coefficient orders under discussion, with no cosmological term.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Expanding $\det\gamma=\det q$ through order $r^{-2}$ gives $q^{AB}C_{AB}=0$ and $q^{AB}P_{AB}=\tfrac12C^2$. Differentiating the latter coefficient identity in $u$ yields $q^{AB}\dot P_{AB}-C^{AB}N_{AB}=0$. The inverse angular metric is $\gamma^{AB}=q^{AB}-C^{AB}/r+(C^A{}_EC^{EB}-P^{AB})/r^2+O(r^{-3})$. These expansions retain the subleading trace fixed by determinant gauge.

Inverting the Bondi-Sachs block metric gives $g^{ur}=-e^{-2\beta}$, $g^{rr}=e^{-2\beta}V/r$, $g^{rA}=-e^{-2\beta}U^A$, and $g^{AB}=r^{-2}\gamma^{AB}$, with $g^{uu}=g^{uA}=0$. Multiplication by the metric components in [F1] verifies each identity.

Substitution of this Bondi metric into the Christoffel and Ricci formulas [F2]–[F3] gives the exact radial component
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{rr}=\frac4r\partial_r\beta-\frac14\gamma^{AC}\gamma^{BD}(\partial_r\gamma_{AB})(\partial_r\gamma_{CD}).$$
Thus [A2] implies $\partial_r\beta=\tfrac r{16}\gamma^{AC}\gamma^{BD}(\partial_r\gamma_{AB})(\partial_r\gamma_{CD})$. From [F1], $\partial_r\gamma_{AB}=-C_{AB}/r^2+O(r^{-3})$ and $\gamma^{AB}=q^{AB}+O(r^{-1})$, so the right side is $C^2/(16r^3)+O(r^{-4})$. Integrating in $r$ with $\beta\to0$ gives $\beta=-C^2/(32r^2)+O(r^{-3})$.

The vacuum $rA$ hypersurface equation obtained from [F2]–[F3] is
$$\partial_r(r^4e^{-2\beta}\gamma_{AB}\partial_rU^B)=2r^4\partial_r(r^{-2}\mathcal D_A\beta)-r^2\gamma^{EF}\mathcal D_E(\partial_r\gamma_{AF}),$$
where $\mathcal D$ is the Levi-Civita derivative of $\gamma$ on a fixed $r,u$ sphere. If $U^A=U^A_{(2)}r^{-2}+O(r^{-3})$, the left side is $-2q_{AB}U^B_{(2)}+O(r^{-1})$. By [F1] and step 1.3, the right side is $D^BC_{AB}+O(r^{-1})$: the $\beta$ term is $O(r^{-1})$, while $\partial_r\gamma_{AF}=-C_{AF}r^{-2}+O(r^{-3})$. Equality of the constant coefficients yields $U^A_{(2)}=-\tfrac12D_BC^{AB}$. This leading solve does not determine the $r^{-3}$ coefficient.

The vacuum radial $V$ equation from [F2]–[F3] is
$$2e^{-2\beta}\partial_rV=\mathcal R[\gamma]-2\gamma^{AB}(\mathcal D_A\mathcal D_B\beta+\mathcal D_A\beta\,\mathcal D_B\beta)+e^{-2\beta}r^{-2}\mathcal D_A\!\left[\partial_r(r^4U^A)\right]-\frac12r^4e^{-4\beta}\gamma_{AB}(\partial_rU^A)(\partial_rU^B),$$
where $\mathcal R[\gamma]$ is the scalar curvature of the cut metric $\gamma_{AB}$. The first variation of scalar curvature at the unit sphere, applied to the trace-free $C_{AB}/r$, gives $\mathcal R[\gamma]=2+r^{-1}D_AD_BC^{AB}+O(r^{-2})$. From step 2.1, $r^{-2}D_A\partial_r(r^4U^A)=2r^{-1}D_AU^A_{(2)}+O(r^{-2})=-r^{-1}D_AD_BC^{AB}+O(r^{-2})$. The $r^{-1}$ terms cancel; the other displayed terms are $O(r^{-2})$, so $\partial_rV=1+O(r^{-2})$. Integration and $V/r\to1$ give $V=r+V_{(0)}+O(r^{-1})$, where the definition in [F1] identifies $V_{(0)}=-2m$.

The planned final calculation must expand every $r^{-2}$ contribution to $\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}$ after the radial solves, including the trace-free part of $P_{AB}$ and the coefficients $U^A_{(3)},V_{(1)},\beta_{(3)}$. The literature records that these terms reduce to [L1], but this draft does not supply the contraction and cancellation showing that reduction. In particular, [L1] is the exact unresolved step; the preceding leading radial solves do not prove it.

Conditional on the unresolved coefficient identity [L1], vacuum [A2] makes that coefficient zero. Rearranging and using $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}$ gives $\partial_um=\tfrac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\tfrac18N_{AB}N^{AB}$. This establishes the target only once [L1] has a complete local proof; until then this is an explicit conditional reduction.

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart $x$ and metric components
$\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$
([[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Since the chart identifies each
$T_p\mathbb R^4$ with $\mathbb R^4$, all objects below are defined by their
components in this chart; they are the components at a point, and a subscript
$p$ is suppressed. Indices are raised and lowered with $\eta$ and $\eta^{-1}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]), and orthogonality is in
the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]].

**(a) Observer, propagation direction, screen.** Let $n=n^a\partial_a$ be an
**observer** of the flat model: $n$ is future-directed, $\eta(n,n)=-1$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); and let
$s=s^a\partial_a$ be a **propagation direction**: $\eta(s,s)=1$ and
$\eta(n,s)=0$. The pair defines the two-dimensional **screen**
$\Sigma(n,s):=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:\eta(v,n)=0,\ \eta(v,s)=0\}$, on which the
restriction of $\eta$ is positive definite by
[[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The **screen projector** and
the **spatial projector** of the pair are the $(1,1)$-tensors with components

$$p^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b-s^as_b,\qquad h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,$$

and the covariant form of the screen projector is
$p_{ab}:=\eta_{ac}p^c{}_b=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b-s_as_b$. The properties $p^2=p$,
$h^2=h$, $\operatorname{im}p=\Sigma(n,s)$ and $\operatorname{im}h=n^\perp$
are proved in the screen-projector lemma of this page.

**(b) TT projection.** Let $A=(A_{ab})$ be a symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
at a point. Its **transverse-traceless (TT) projection with respect to
$(n,s)$** is the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor

$$\Pi_{n,s}(A)_{ab}:=p_a{}^cp_b{}^dA_{cd}-\tfrac12\,p_{ab}\,p^{cd}A_{cd},\qquad p^{cd}:=\eta^{ce}\eta^{df}p_{ef}.$$

**(c) Screen amplitudes.** Let $(e_1,e_2)$ be an ordered
$\eta$-orthonormal basis of $\Sigma(n,s)$ (which exists by
[[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]] applied
to the positive-definite restriction of $\eta$). For a symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor $A$ the **plus and cross amplitudes of $A$ with respect to
$(e_1,e_2)$** are $A_+:=A(e_1,e_1)$ and $A_\times:=A(e_1,e_2)$; if $A$ is
TT with respect to $(n,s)$ in the sense of clause (d) below, then, extending
the screen dual basis to covectors on $\mathbb R^4$ by
$e^i(v):=\eta(e_i,v)$ for $i=1,2$ (so both vanish on $n,s$),

$$A=A_+\bigl(e^1\otimes e^1-e^2\otimes e^2\bigr)+A_\times\bigl(e^1\otimes e^2+e^2\otimes e^1\bigr).$$

For a TT screen tensor $A$, under the rotation
$e_1'=\cos\theta\,e_1+\sin\theta\,e_2$,
$e_2'=-\sin\theta\,e_1+\cos\theta\,e_2$ of the screen basis the amplitudes
transform as $A_+'=A_+\cos2\theta+A_\times\sin2\theta$ and
$A_\times'=-A_+\sin2\theta+A_\times\cos2\theta$. Here $\sin$ and $\cos$
are the power-series functions of [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]];
expanding $A(e_1',e_1')$ and $A(e_1',e_2')$ by bilinearity and applying the
addition formulas of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]] gives the two
displayed transformations.

**(d) TT tensors and TT perturbations.** A symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
$A$ is **transverse-traceless (TT) with respect to $(n,s)$** when
$A(n,\cdot)=0$, $A(s,\cdot)=0$ and $\eta^{ab}A_{ab}=0$. For a symmetric
field $h$ on a nonempty open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, use the
constant smooth extensions of the fixed component vectors:
$n_q:=n^a\partial_a|_q$ and $s_q:=s^a\partial_a|_q$ for $q\in\Omega$.
Here a symmetric field is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field with symmetric
components in the sense of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then
"TT with respect to $(n,s)$" means
$h_q(n_q,\cdot)=h_q(s_q,\cdot)=0$ and $\eta^{ab}h_{ab}(q)=0$ for every
$q\in\Omega$. It is **spatial with respect to $n$** when
$h_q(n_q,\cdot)=0$ for every $q\in\Omega$.

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the screen, the two projections and the
amplitude terminology, and states the rotation law of clause (c) as part of
the naming. It asserts no property of $\Pi_{n,s}$ (idempotence, rank, image
and trace are proved in the screen-projector lemma of this page), no relation
to the planar perturbations of the plane-wave definition of this page
(established in the gauge-decomposition lemma of this page) and no physical
interpretation of the amplitudes.

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart and let $(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ be a flat linearized family over
an open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ with first-order coefficients
$\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}$ as in [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]; write
$R^a{}_{bcd}(\lambda)$ for the curvature components of $g(\lambda)$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]) and define the
**first-order curvature coefficient**

$$R^{(1)a}{}_{bcd}:=\partial_\lambda R^a{}_{bcd}(\lambda)\big|_{\lambda=0},\qquad R^{(1)}_{abcd}:=\eta_{ae}R^{(1)e}{}_{bcd}.$$

Then:

**(a) General first-order formula.** The coefficient is defined (the
component family is differentiable in $\lambda$ at $0$) and

$$R^{(1)a}{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{cb},\qquad R^{(1)}_{abcd}=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_b\partial_ch_{ad}+\partial_a\partial_dh_{bc}-\partial_a\partial_ch_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dh_{ac}\bigr).$$

**(b) Gauge invariance.** For every smooth covector field $\xi$ on $\Omega$,
with $h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$ the gauge-transformed
perturbation of [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clause (d),
$R^{(1)}_{abcd}(h')=R^{(1)}_{abcd}(h)$: the first-order curvature coefficient
is unchanged by gauge transformations.

**(c) Planar and TT waves.** Let $F=(F_{ab})$ be a smooth planar profile with
$h_{ab}(x)=F_{ab}(u(x))$, $u=x^0-x^3$, and let $n_a=\partial_au$; then

$$R^{(1)}_{abcd}=\tfrac12\bigl(n_bn_cF''_{ad}+n_an_dF''_{bc}-n_an_cF''_{bd}-n_bn_dF''_{ac}\bigr).$$

If the profile is spatial ($F_{0a}=0$ for all $a$), then
$R^{(1)}_{0i0j}=-\tfrac12F''_{ij}$ and, raising indices,
$R^{(1)i}{}_{00j}=+\tfrac12F''{}^i{}_j$. If the profile is TT with amplitudes
$A_+,A_\times$, then $F''$ is supported on the screen with $F''_{11}=A_+''$,
$F''_{22}=-A_+''$, $F''_{12}=F''_{21}=A_\times''$ and all other second
derivatives of the profile zero; in particular

$$R^{(1)}_{0101}=-\tfrac12A_+'',\qquad R^{(1)}_{0102}=-\tfrac12A_\times'',\qquad R^{(1)}_{0202}=+\tfrac12A_+'' .$$

**(d) Contraction to the Ricci coefficient.** For every perturbation $h$,

$$\eta^{ac}R^{(1)}_{abcd}=\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{bd},$$

the right-hand side being the first-order coefficient of

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $R$ be its
curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$I,J_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be intervals with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]), and let $F:J_0\times I\to M$ be a smooth map. Write
$T:=\partial_tF$ and $J^F:=\partial_rF$; a field along $F$ means a smooth
section of $F^*TM$ over $J_0\times I$, and $D_r,D_t$ are the covariant
derivatives in the two parameters
([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

field $V$ along $F$,
$$\bigl(D_tD_r-D_rD_t\bigr)V=R(T,J^F)V .$$

**(b) Geodesic deviation.** Suppose in addition that for every $r\in J_0$ the
curve $t\mapsto F(r,t)$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $t$, that is
$D_tT=0$. Then $D_tJ^F=D_rT$ and
$$D_t^2J^F=R(T,J^F)T .$$
Consequently, for every $r$ the field $t\mapsto J^F(r,t)$ is a Jacobi field
along the geodesic $t\mapsto F(r,t)$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)), and for a geodesic
variation the variation field is a Jacobi field.

**(c) Initial data.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth geodesic and let
$s_0\in I$. For every pair $J_0,J_1\in T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$ there exists exactly
one smooth Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ with
$$J(s_0)=J_0,\qquad D_sJ(s_0)=J_1 .$$

dimension $8$, and $J\mapsto\bigl(J(s_0),D_sJ(s_0)\bigr)$ is a linear
isomorphism onto $T_{\gamma(s_0)}M\oplus T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$.

smooth Jacobi field along it. Then $s\mapsto g(J,\gamma')(s)$ is affine, and
if $\gamma$ is future timelike with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-1$, the normal
component $J^\perp$ of [[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $G : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at every
point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ (The derivative $f'(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c}$ of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point $c \in A$ that is a limit point of $A$, and differentiability on a set; at $a$ and $b$
this is the one-sided derivative), let $f := G'$, and suppose $f$ is integrable
on $[a,b]$ (The lower and upper Darboux integrals of a bounded $f$ on $[a,b]$ as $\sup_P L(f,P)$ and $\inf_P U(f,P)$, Darboux integrability as their equality, and the notation $\int_a^b f$). Then

$$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**Both hypotheses are needed and neither is removable.** A function may be
differentiable everywhere with $G'$ not integrable — then the left-hand side does
not exist (an everywhere differentiable function with unbounded derivative) — and an
integrable $f$ need not be the derivative of anything
(the sign function); both witnesses are on the
companion page.

**No continuity of $f$ is assumed**, which is what makes this the working form:
the theorem evaluates $\int_a^b f$ for every integrable derivative, not only for
continuous integrands.

Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian tangent-bundle conventions of the suppliers. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, $r_0>0$, and $\mathcal E=I\times(r_0,\infty)\times S^2$, where $S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ has its unit round metric $q_{AB}$ and area form $d\Omega$. Let $D_A$ be the Levi-Civita covariant derivative of $q$, and raise angular indices with $q^{AB}$. A **Bondi-Sachs end** is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $\mathcal E$ written in coordinates $(u,r,x^A)$, $A,B=1,2$, as

$$g=-\left(e^{2\beta}\frac Vr-r^2\gamma_{AB}U^AU^B\right)du^2-2e^{2\beta}du\,dr-2r^2\gamma_{AB}U^Bdu\,dx^A+r^2\gamma_{AB}dx^A dx^B,$$

where $\beta,V,U^A,\gamma_{AB}$ are smooth, $\gamma_{AB}$ is positive definite, $\gamma^{AC}\gamma_{CB}=\delta^A_B$, and $\det(\gamma_{AB})=\det(q_{AB})$. Thus $u=\mathrm{constant}$ are outgoing null hypersurfaces, $r$ is the area radius, and $x^A$ are constant along their null generators. This Bondi gauge has $g_{rr}=g_{rA}=0$.

A **smooth Bondi expansion** is such an end with the differentiated uniform expansions

$$\gamma_{AB}=q_{AB}+\frac{C_{AB}(u,x)}r+\frac{P_{AB}(u,x)}{r^2}+O(r^{-3}),\qquad \beta=O(r^{-2}),\qquad U^A=\frac{U^A_{(2)}(u,x)}{r^2}+\frac{U^A_{(3)}(u,x)}{r^3}+O(r^{-4}),\qquad V=r-2m(u,x)+\frac{V_{(1)}(u,x)}r+O(r^{-2}).$$

Here $C_{AB}$, $P_{AB}$ and the displayed coefficients are smooth sphere fields on $I$; the determinant gauge imposes $q^{AB}C_{AB}=0$ and $q^{AB}P_{AB}=\tfrac12 C_{AB}C^{AB}$. For every compact $I'\subset I$, angular chart compact set, and derivative multi-index $\alpha$ of total order at most two, the partial derivatives of each $O(r^{-k})$ remainder obey $\partial_u^{\alpha_u}D^{\alpha_x}\partial_r^{\alpha_r}O(r^{-k})=O(r^{-k-\alpha_r})$ uniformly as $r\to\infty$. Define the **mass aspect** $m$ by the $r^{-1}$ coefficient in $V$, the **Bondi shear** by $C_{AB}=\lim_{r\to\infty}r(\gamma_{AB}-q_{AB})$, the **Bondi news** by $N_{AB}:=\partial_u C_{AB}$, and the **geometric Bondi mass** by $m_B(u):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}m(u,x)\,d\Omega$. The future null boundary used here is the formal $r\to\infty$ boundary $\mathcal I^+=I\times S^2$ with coordinates $(u,x^A)$; no conformal completion is included in this definition. A **vacuum Bondi expansion** means, in addition, that the Ricci tensor $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ defined by the curvature convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] vanishes to the asymptotic coefficient orders under discussion, with no cosmological term.

derivations.claim: For fixed $u\in I$, define the smooth sphere vector field $X^A:=D_BN^{AB}$. In standard spherical coordinates $q=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, its divergence satisfies $D_AX^A\,d\Omega=\{\partial_\theta(\sin\theta X^\theta)+\partial_\phi(\sin\theta X^\phi)\}\,d\theta\,d\phi$. The $\phi$-boundary terms cancel by periodicity. Smoothness makes $X^\theta$ bounded in norm near each pole, so $\sin\theta X^\theta\to0$ at $\theta=0,\pi$; hence $\int_{S^2}D_AD_BN^{AB}\,d\Omega=0$.

Smoothness on each compact $u$-slab permits differentiation under the finite sphere integral: for small $h$, the difference quotient for $m_B$ equals $\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}\int_0^1\partial_um(u+th,x)\,dt\,d\Omega$, and uniform continuity of $\partial_um$ makes it converge uniformly in $x$ to $\frac1{4\pi}\partial_um(u,x)$. Therefore $\frac{dm_B}{du}=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}\partial_um\,d\Omega$.

Substitute [F2] into step 1.2 and use step 1.1 to eliminate the double divergence. The remaining term is $-\frac1{32\pi}\int_{S^2}N_{AB}N^{AB}\,d\Omega$, proving the equality. Since $q$ is positive definite, $N_{AB}N^{AB}=|N|_q^2\ge0$ pointwise, proving the inequality.

If $dm_B/du=0$ at a fixed $u\in J$, step 2.1 gives the integral of the continuous nonnegative function $|N|_q^2$ equal to zero. If $N$ were nonzero at some point, continuity and positive definiteness of $q$ would make $|N|_q^2$ strictly positive on a sphere neighborhood of positive area, contradicting the zero integral. Thus $N=0$ on that cut; applying this to every $u\in J$ proves the final claim.

derivations.claim: The scalar $Y$ is smooth because it is the restriction of a polynomial on $\mathbb R^3$. By contraction, $q^{AB}T_{AB}=D^2Y-\tfrac12(2)D^2Y=0$. In spherical coordinates at the equator $\theta=\pi/2$, $D_\theta D_\theta Y=3$, $D_\phi D_\phi Y=0$, and $D^2Y=3$, so $T_{\theta\theta}=3/2\ne0$. Thus $T$ is a nonzero smooth trace-free tensor.

Define $b(u)=e^{-1/(1-u^2)}$ for $|u|<1$ and $b(u)=0$ for $|u|\ge1$, let $Z=\int_{-1}^{1}b(u)\,du>0$, and set $g=b/Z$. Every derivative of the interior formula is a polynomial in $(1-u^2)^{-1}$ and $u$ times $e^{-1/(1-u^2)}$, which tends to zero at both endpoints; hence the zero extension is smooth on $\mathbb R$, has support $[-1,1]$, is nonnegative, and has integral one. The function $H(u)=\int_{-\infty}^u g$ is smooth, equals $0$ for $u\le-1$, equals $1$ for $u\ge1$, and $H'=g$.

The fields $C_{AB}=aHT_{AB}$ and $N_{AB}=agT_{AB}$ are smooth and trace-free, and $N=\partial_uC$. Therefore $\Delta C_{AB}=aT_{AB}$ by the normalization $\int g=1$. Define $m(u,x)$ from $m(-1,x)=0$ by integrating the right side of the local mass-aspect equation in [F2]; its integrand is smooth, so this gives smooth formal Bondi mass-aspect data satisfying that constraint.

Applying [F2] over $[-1,1]$ gives the displayed mass change. The first integral is positive because $g$ is continuous and has unit integral; the sphere integral is positive because $q$ is positive definite and $T$ is continuous and nonzero by step 1.1. Since $a\ne0$, the mass change is strictly negative.

The pulse has $N(-1)=N(1)=0$, so [F3] applies. Its integrated shear change is $\Delta C=aT$, hence the leading detector displacement is $\Delta s^A=\tfrac{a}{2r}T^A{}_Bs^B+O(r^{-2}|s|)+O(\varepsilon^2|s|)$, with exactly the stated finite-radius and nonlinear qualifications.

Let a vacuum Bondi expansion be as in [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]], with $R_{ab}=0$ in the curvature convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then, for the mass aspect $m$, shear $C_{AB}$, news $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}$, unit sphere metric $q_{AB}$ and its Levi-Civita derivative $D_A$ specified there,

$$\partial_um=\frac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\frac18N_{AB}N^{AB}.$$

The identity is the leading supplementary vacuum Einstein coefficient at future null infinity; it is not an exact finite-radius equation.

Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian sphere-bundle convention of [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. Let a smooth vacuum Bondi expansion be defined on an open retarded-length interval $I$. Then

$$\frac{dm_B}{du}=-\frac1{32\pi}\int_{S^2}N_{AB}N^{AB}\,d\Omega\le0.$$

If $dm_B/du=0$ throughout an open subinterval $J\subset I$ and $N_{AB}$ is continuous on $J\times S^2$, then $N_{AB}=0$ on $J\times S^2$.

Assume Countable Choice and a smooth Bondi expansion as in [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. For $u_1<u_2$ in its retarded-length interval, define $\Delta C_{AB}:=C_{AB}(u_2)-C_{AB}(u_1)$. Then

$$\Delta C_{AB}=\int_{u_1}^{u_2}N_{AB}(u)\,du.$$

For the detector clause, fix an angular point and a large fixed area radius $r$. Use the local flat observer and propagation direction of [[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]] to identify the positive two-dimensional screen. A **linear transverse detector approximation** here means that the dimensionless screen metric perturbation is $H_{AB}(u)=C_{AB}(u,x)/r+\rho_{AB}(u,r,x)$, where the screen-TT remainder and its first two $u$-derivatives are $O(r^{-2})$ uniformly on $[u_1,u_2]$; retain only first order in $H$ and first order in separation. Let $s^A(u)$ be the screen Jacobi field of a smooth timelike geodesic variation, with affine parameter $u$ (equivalently $x^0=ct=u+r$ along the background central geodesic), initial data $s^A(u_1)=s^A$ and $\partial_us^A(u_1)=0$, and assume $N_{AB}(u_1)=N_{AB}(u_2)=0$. Then, at this linear separation order,

$$s^A(u_2)-s^A(u_1)=\frac{1}{2r}\Delta C^A{}_B\,s^B+O(r^{-2}|s|)+O(\varepsilon^2|s|),\qquad \varepsilon:=\sup_{[u_1,u_2]}|H|_q.$$

Under the same approximation, the endpoint relative screen velocity satisfies $\partial_us^A(u_2)=O(r^{-2}|s|)+O(\varepsilon^2|s|)$, so it has no leading $r^{-1}$ contribution when the news vanishes at both cuts.

The error constants depend on the fixed compact interval, angular patch and differentiated remainder bounds in [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. No exact finite-radius identity $H_{AB}=C_{AB}/r$ is asserted.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The restriction $Y=\tfrac12(3x_3^2-1)$ is smooth on the sphere because it is the restriction of a polynomial. Put $T_{AB}:=D_AD_BY-\tfrac12q_{AB}D^2Y$. Its trace is zero. At $\theta=\pi/2$, $D_\theta D_\theta Y=3$, $D_\phi D_\phi Y=0$ and $D^2Y=3$, so $T_{\theta\theta}=3/2$; hence $T$ is nonzero.

Since Y is independent of u, [F2] gives C_AB=delta_f C_AB=-2aT_AB, independent of u and nonzero; [F1] then gives N_AB=0. The data are formal infinitesimal boundary data, so no nonlinear finite transformation is asserted.

Substitution of $N_{AB}=0$ in [F3] gives $\partial_um=0$, and [F4] gives $dm_B/du=0$. For every $u_1<u_2$, [F5] gives $\Delta C_{AB}=\int_{u_1}^{u_2}0\,du=0$ and hence zero leading memory displacement. Thus the static nonzero shear has no news flux and no shear change.
